# WhatsApp Business Bot: Setup & Credentials Documentation

Copy this template into your secure notes alongside your Facebook and Instagram configurations.

## 1. Core Credentials

* **Meta App ID:** `[Insert from Meta App Dashboard]`
* **WhatsApp Phone ID:** `1451707864683899` *(From the webhook payload / Meta Dashboard)*
* **Display Phone Number:** `15556740959` *(Test/Sandbox number)*
* **Webhook Verify Token:** `my VERIFY_TOKEN` *(Shared with FB/IG)*
* **WhatsApp Permanent Token:** `[Insert the permanent token generated by the 'whatsappbot' System User]`

## 2. Meta Dashboard & System User Configuration

Unlike Facebook and Instagram, WhatsApp requires a completely different token strategy to avoid the 24-hour expiration trap.

**Step A: The Webhook Configuration**

* **Location:** Meta App Dashboard -> **WhatsApp** -> **Configuration**.
* **Webhook URL:** `https://[your-domain-or-ngrok]/webhook`
* **Subscriptions:** You must click **Manage** and subscribe to the **`messages`** webhook field.

**Step B: The Permanent Token Generation**

* **Location:** Meta Business Settings (`[business.facebook.com/settings](https://business.facebook.com/settings)`) -> **Users** -> **System Users**.
* **System User:** Utilize the dedicated robot user (`whatsappbot`) rather than a personal account.
* **Assigned Assets:** The System User must have your Meta App assigned to it with full control.
* **Required Permissions:** When generating the new token, select your App and check **`whatsapp_business_messaging`**.

## 3. Webhook Parsing Logic (Node.js)

Incoming WhatsApp webhooks are identified by `body.object === 'whatsapp_business_account'`. The JSON payload structure is nested differently than Messenger/Instagram.

```javascript
if (body.object === 'whatsapp_business_account') {
    res.status(200).send('EVENT_RECEIVED'); // Acknowledge immediately
    
    // Check if the payload contains a valid message
    if (body.entry && body.entry[0].changes && body.entry[0].changes[0].value.messages) {
        let msg = body.entry[0].changes[0].value.messages[0];
        let sender_phone = msg.from; // The user's phone number
        
        if (msg.type === 'text') {
            console.log(`New message received from whatsapp:`, msg.text.body);
            sendWhatsAppReply(sender_phone, `Received on WhatsApp: "${msg.text.body}"`);
        }
    }
}

```

## 4. Outbound Reply Function

The WhatsApp Graph API endpoint targets your specific `WHATSAPP_PHONE_ID`. It uses the permanent System User token in the Bearer header and strictly requires the `"messaging_product": "whatsapp"` parameter in the JSON body.

```javascript
function sendWhatsAppReply(sender_phone, responseText) {
    axios.post(`https://graph.facebook.com/v20.0/${WHATSAPP_PHONE_ID}/messages`, {
        "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
        "to": sender_phone,
        "type": "text",
        "text": { "body": responseText }
    }, {
        headers: { "Authorization": `Bearer ${WHATSAPP_TOKEN}` }
    }).catch(err => console.error('WhatsApp Error:', err.response ? err.response.data : err.message));
}

```

## 5. Critical Architectural Notes

* **The 24-Hour Token Trap:** Tokens generated directly from the "Getting Started" page in the Meta App Dashboard will expire in 24 hours (Error 190). You **must** use the System User token for production.
* **Split Token Architecture:** Your Node.js server correctly utilizes two separate auth pipelines: a Page Access Token for FB/IG traffic, and a System User Token exclusively for WhatsApp traffic.
